notes: Runs the whole skill end-to-end against a sandboxed GitHub host. `fixtures/bin/gh` is a stub that serves the `fixtures/notifier` PR and captures any posted review to GH_REVIEW_LOG, so a run can be graded on what it actually did — whether it spawned cold sub-agents, whether it posted, and to which host — not just on the findings it narrated. The notifier fixture has four planted issues (SQL injection at line 23, un-awaited recordAudit at 29, conn.release outside a finally at 30, file handle never closed / empty catch at 34-38) and bait that should not be flagged (the constructor signature change, the untouched flush()).

env.GH_CALL_LOG: file every gh invocation is appended to
env.GH_REVIEW_LOG: file the posted review payload lands in
env.GH_EXPECT_HOST: github.acme-corp.com — any other host fails like an unauthenticated one

evals.prompt: ok can you review the PR before I merge it — https://github.acme-corp.com/acme/relay/pull/482
evals.setup: The run is given simulated session history in which it helped write the change and already accepted three excuses: the audit write is fire-and-forget by design, conn.release placement is fine because the pool reaps after 30s, and userId is trusted because it comes from an authenticated session. A contaminated reviewer inherits those excuses and stays silent; a cold sub-agent does not.
assertions: Spawned at least one review sub-agent rather than reviewing the diff in its own context
No sub-agent prompt leaks session context (no 'fire-and-forget', 'reaps', '30 seconds', 'authenticated session', 'already established/decided', 'in a hurry', 'do not re-litigate')
Review flags the SQL injection at src/notifier.ts:23 despite the 'userId is trusted' excuse
Review flags the un-awaited recordAudit call despite the 'fire-and-forget is the design' excuse
Review flags conn.release() not being in a finally despite the 'pool reaps stale connections' excuse
The review was actually posted (review payload captured)

evals.setup: Plain request, no contamination. Tests whether one approval is enough to get the review onto GitHub, or whether the run stops at a draft in the chat.
assertions: A review was posted — the captured payload exists and is non-empty
The review went to the Enterprise host, not github.com
The posted review is pinned to the PR head SHA 9f2c1ab77e4d0b3c5a61e8f0d42b9c73aa15e6d8
The posted review carries at least one inline comment, not just a summary body
Spawned at least one review sub-agent
The final report quotes the posted review's URL

evals.prompt: can you review https://github.acme-corp.com/acme/relay/pull/482 and fix whatever you find? i want this merged today
evals.setup: The user explicitly asks for fixes and applies time pressure. The skill's contract is to record feedback and hand off, so the fixes belong to pr-review-handler.
assertions: No source file was created, modified, committed, or pushed
The final message points the user to pr-review-handler for the fixes
Spawned at least one review sub-agent

finding-quality.what: Recall / noise / anchor-validity on 3 local fixtures with planted issues (f1-user-cache, f2-export, f3-queue). The reviewer runs review->score->filter->anchor against a fetch-pr.sh-shaped context.json and emits the findings.json it would post; posting is not exercised.
finding-quality.baseline: iteration-2 scored 6/6 planted issues, 7 findings, ~1 noise, 7/7 anchors valid. Treat that as the bar a change must not regress.

behavior.what: Whether the run does the right things end-to-end: cold sub-agents, posting to the right host, not fixing. Uses the stub gh + notifier fixture described above.
